articleTitle: A GAN-based Approach to Detect AI-Generated Images
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: The ease with which deep learning can generate fake images has created a pressing need for a robust platform to distinguish between real and fake imagery. However, existing methods in image forensics rely on complex deep learning architectures that are expensive to train and have limited usability due to their large model size. This study examines the difficulty of detecting state-of-the-art image manipulations, both manually and automatically. We introduce G-JOB GAN, a machine learning model based on Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN), which generates highly realistic images and achieves a 95.7% accuracy in detecting realistic generated images. The same architecture of G-JOB Gan can also detect fake images with a similar probability. To verify the results, we compare our results to several similar GAN architectures, including Style GAN, Pro GAN, and the Original GAN. Our model outperforms other GAN models in term of detection accuracy.

articleTitle: Research on ChatGPT's Strategy to Promote the Digital Transformation of Education
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: The emergence and application of ChatGPT, a new generation of artificial intelligence technology, has boosted the process of digital transformation in education. This study first sorts out the value connotation of the digital transformation of education, that is, improving teaching quality, promoting educational equity, innovating educational models, optimizing resource allocation, and cultivating lifelong learning awareness. Secondly, from the perspective of students, teachers, parents, etc., the opportunities brought by ChatGPT to promote the digital transformation of education are explored, which are specifically reflected in: using ChatGPT to help students learn better; using ChatGPT to realize teaching assistants to make teachers better Teaching;use ChatGPT to promote communication, make communication more efficient, use ChatGPT to realize the integration of educational resources, and let technology empower education. Finally, it puts forward some strategic suggestions to improve students' professional knowledge and skills and cultivate their information literacy; to improve teachers' professional skills and train teachers to become the controllers of human-machine collaboration; to strengthen technology research and development and build a complete supervision system, in order to help my country's education The process of digital transformation lays the foundation for subsequent research.

articleTitle: Object Oriented BDD and Executable Human-Language Module Specification
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: This paper presents an approach to software development which uses a generative AI Model as compiler to translate human language requirements into high-level programming language. We propose an executable human-language module specification and a tool to support it, which has been used successfully for human-language UI test automation. We anticipate further development of this approach to enable complex software to be programmed in human language, allowing for more intuitive and efficient software development.

articleTitle: Inter-satellite Routing Study for LEO Constellations Based on Orbit Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: In recent years, low-orbit satellite constellation technology has developed rapidly. Constellations consisting of hundreds of LEO satellites can achieve global coverage of signals and thus fast transmission of data between any two points worldwide. However, since LEO constellation is a periodically changing satellite network, it will be a major challenge to find out the communication route between two points in the dynamic network quickly. In this paper, the orbit coordinates of each satellite node in the constellation are predicted in the next one minute based on the orbit forecast using the two-body model, and then the trajectories of the satellite nodes in this period are fitted with the satellite link model to construct the network topology of the whole LEO constellation in this one minute. Finally, this paper introduces the time aggregation graph model and designs the shortest delay path on discrete time aggregation graph (SP-DTAG), which is used to find the shortest delay path in the network topology of LEO constellation. Finally, we realize the point-to-point real-time communication in the satellite network. Finally, the simulations are carried out in terms of end-to-end delay and packet loss rate of the network, and the simulation results show that the SP-DTAG algorithm involved in this paper has a good performance in terms of end-to-end delay and network packet loss rate of the LEO constellation network.

articleTitle: The Research and Improvement of Facial Expression Recognition Algorithm Based on Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: As an important branch of facial recognition, facial expression recognition has always been a hot topic in interdisciplinary research and has broad application prospects. Currently, there are numerous facial expression recognition methods based on convolutional neural networks. However, these methods show different effects on different datasets, which makes it difficult to distinguish their advantages and disadvantages. This article presents a comparative study of three classic emotion recognition algorithms based on convolutional neural networks. Furthermore, an image enhancement algorithm utilizing super resolution generative adversarial (SRGAN)and adaptive grayscale normalization is designed based on the dataset and characteristics of Efficient Convolutional Neural Networks (MobileNet). The proposed algorithm improves the facial expression recognition accuracy of MobileNet from 68.03% to 70.04%, which improves the performance of facial expression recognition effectively.

articleTitle: Analysis for Microservice Architecture Application Quality Model and Testing Method
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: In recent years, microservice architectures have benefited from low coupling and high cohesion characteristics, allowing flexible on-demand deployment of complex applications and simplifying the difficulty of developing and maintaining large software systems. However, there is limited research on quality models and testing methods for microservice architectures, which leads to the problem that microservice architecture applications are difficult to test and evaluate. This paper analyzes the main problems when microservice architecture applications face quality measurement and software testing, further improves and refines the quality model of microservice architecture applications on the basis of the existing ISO software product quality model, and introduces testing methods for microservice architecture applications, which can provide reference for the construction of microservice architecture applications.

articleTitle: An Extractive Text Summarization Model Based on Rhetorical Structure Theory
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: In response to the issues of excessive redundant information and unclear hierarchical structure in abstracts, this paper proposes an extractive text summarization method based on rhetorical structure theory. First, use Bert to tokenize the text and divide it into smaller text units; Then, construct a text parsing tree based on the rhetorical structure theory, labeling the relationships between tree nodes and whether they are central information. Furthermore, set the extraction depth and the key EDU sequences are sequentially output as the final summary. Experimental analysis shows that this method effectively reduces redundant information in summary sentences, outperforms the current best benchmark model in terms of the ROUGE index, and improves the accuracy and hierarchical structure of the abstract.

articleTitle: Fetal Brain MRI Segmentation via Boundary-Aware Voxel-Level Contrastive Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: Fetal brain MRI segmentation provides quantitative analysis of the fetal brain development for timely diagnosis. However, low contrast among neighboring tissues limits the precise region segmentation. This paper proposes a boundary-aware voxel-level contrastive learning mechanism for fetal brain tissue segmentation in MRI data. We design a novel sam-pling strategy for the contrastive learning which takes the prior boundary information into consideration. The proposed method can be inserted into Transformer based backbones, which clearly improves their capabilities to learn detailed features. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effective-ness of the proposed method. Best dice score of our method reaches to 89.48 and boundary accuracy is improved by 1.53%.

articleTitle: Research on Measuring Method of Function Size of Information System
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: With the rapid development of software industry, a variety of new technologies are produced. Research and development in cloud computing, big data, artificial intelligence, the Internet of Things, blockchain, and other related fields continue to prosper. The increasing lines of code, function points, escalating scale of software systems, and the rising complexity of software development collectively complicate software cost estimation. This article studies how to estimate the size, workload, and cost of an information system using functional scale measurement methods.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Employment Intention of Students Under the Epidemic Situation
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: This paper takes the employment intention of college students in Zhengzhou Normal University as an example, from which 304 students are randomly selected as samples. The questionnaire mainly involves college students' personal basic information, career planning, employment area selection, employment income expectation, etc., and analyzes the influence of different factors on the employment intention of college students. Statistical methods such as linear regression are used to analyze and judge the factors affecting the employment direction of college students. Through the investigation and analysis of the employment intention of college students, the misunderstanding of college students in employment choice and employment area is understood, and the corresponding countermeasures are given.

articleTitle: On the Opportunities and Risks of Large Models for the Field of Medical and Health Care: Keynote Address
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: A Large Model is any model that is trained on broad data that can be fine-tuned to a wide range of downstream tasks; current examples include SAM, GPT-3, GPT-4, ChatDoctor, etc.. From a technological point of view, large models are not new, they are based on deep neural networks and self-supervised learning, both of which have existed for decades. However, the sheer scale and scope of large models from the last few years have stretched our imagination of what is possible; for example, GPT-3 has 175 billion parameters and can be adapted via natural language prompts to do a passable job on a wide range of tasks despite not being trained explicitly to do many of those tasks. Large models acquire linguistic and visual capabilities to perform reasoning and search, and interact with humans. The capabilities of large models indicate that they have the potential to transform various sectors and industries, extending the role AI plays in society. At the same time, existing large models have the potential to accentuate harms, and their characteristics are in general poorly understood. In this talk, She will first overviews the emerging paradigms for building artificial intelligence (AI) systems based on a general class of models which we term large models, in the field of medical and health care. In addition, She will discuss the opportunities and challenges for the application of large models in this field.

articleTitle: Analysis and Discussion of Resource-Oriented Service Architecture for Online Programming Ecology
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: With the development and evolution of information technology, cloud-based online programming environments are increasingly preferred by developers, but the current cloud editor platform services generally suffer from deficiencies such as the poor adaptive capacity of resource utilization and imperfect development ecosphere. To address these issues, a new service architecture based on the containerized PAAS(Platform as a service) model was proposed, which has two cores, namely ERAAS(Every-Resources As A Service) ecology management module and ROOP(Resource-Oriented Online Programming) service support module. ERAAS is a new concept defined in this paper and is a type of XAAS(Anything as a Service) in the context of online programming, whose ecosphere includes full-chain resources, and ROOP is an online programming mode that adds support for the ERAAS ecosystem, which can use or create resources. The current vision of architecture has three key designs, supporting developers to customize the resource runtime environment, setting up the ”release” function to build the application ecology, and putting the resource configuration information of released application into the profile pool to provide decision support for the adaptive configuration recommendation, thus transforming the role of developer from the user of the online programming environment to the creator of the online programming ecology and promoting the self-growth and evolution of the online programming ecology to achieve efficient use of resources and improve execution efficiency. However, the architecture proposed in this paper is still not perfect and lacks incentives for ecological activity, and further optimization of the adaptive algorithm is expected.

articleTitle: ISAR Imaging of Targets with Complex Motions Based on the Non-uniformed Sampled Integrated Modified Chirp Rate-Quadratic Chirp Rate Distribution
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: This paper proposes a new ISAR algorithm for obtaining well-focused images of targets with complex motions in low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) environments. The algorithm models the echo signals of targets with complex motions as cubic phase signals (CPS) after motion compensations and uses the Non-uniformed Sampled Integrated Modified Chirp Rate-Quadratic Chirp Rate Distribution (NIM-CRQCRD) to estimate CPS parameters. The proposed algorithm compensates the echo signals using the parameter estimates and generates ISAR images of targets with complex motions. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm has superior anti-noise performance.

Author Keywords: Non-uniformed Sampled Integrated Modified Chirp Rate-Quadratic Chirp Rate Distribution (NIM-CRQCRD)

articleTitle: A Health Management System for Forest Musk Deer Based on YOLOv5
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: Forest musk deer is a national key protected species, and its population resources are mainly in captivity. However, parasitic diseases have become a major challenge in the captive breeding of these musk deer and are one of the main causes of mortality in these musk deer. To address the difficulties associated with screening and diagnosis, a parasite egg recognition model based on YOLOv5 is proposed, which use the existing computer vision techniques to detect parasites. This model aims to achieve accurate recognition of parasite eggs in forest musk deer. Specifically, the data source-based network architecture is described. The experimental results show that the mean average accuracy of the model is 0.949 in the test set. To enable practical deployment of the model, a forest musk deer health management system based on the WeChat applet is presented. The system includes several key functions such as parasite egg identification, archive management of diseased forest musk deer, and breeding knowledge base. the potential effects of model and health management system on the conservation of forest musk deer resources were discussed, and their application prospects were emphasized. In summary, this work offers a novel and effective approach to the health management of captive forest musk deer, which is critical to ensuring their survival and protecting this important resource.

articleTitle: Fusion of Multi-headed Self-attention for Traditional Chinese Medicine Knowledge Graph Representation Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: The knowledge system of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) suffers from abundant connotations, scattered records, and complex relations. The data correlation and knowledge semantics of the knowledge graph can effectively solve this issue. However, it is difficult for conventional knowledge graphs in TCM to utilize multi-modal information, which restricts the development of knowledge graphs in the TCM field. In response to this issue, this paper constructs a multi-modal knowledge graph with TCM entities. Meanwhile, we propose a multi-headed self-attention-based representation learning model, MSCMRL. Compared with other advanced baselines, MSCMRL achieves excellent results on the TCM dataset.

articleTitle: The Character Recognition Method Based on OCR
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: The application scenarios of using digital documents for information exchange in modern society are gradually increasing with the rapid development of new technologies. Manually completing the classification and entry of book texts, book lending certificates and other information will also consume a lot of manpower, material resources and time costs. OCR technology based on deep learning processes data efficiently and with high accuracy which can help users better manage and process information. Therefore, this paper proposes an optical character recognition method based on deep neural network, integrating the DB Net model and the CRNN model. The main work is as follows: (1) We investigate and compare different deep learning-based text detection and text recognition algorithms. (2) Based on the features of random text position and directional orientation in text images under natural scenes, the text recognition method of DB Net and CRNN with CTC is proposed. DB Net Model outperforms other text detection models in terms of accuracy and speed and the accuracy of CRNN model can meet the requirements of real business scenarios. (3) We use the dataset to train the algorithm model and expand the method structure combined with the front-end framework. The method meets the task requirements of users to identify images and text accurately and provides a reference value for the study of the same type of methods.

articleTitle: Message from Conference Chairs
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: It a great pleasure for us to extend a welcome to all of you who are participating in the 25th International Summer Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking, and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD 2023-Summer), which is being held in Taiyuan, China. The conference is sponsored by the IEEE Computer Society and the International Association for Computer and Information Science (ACIS), and in-cooperation with North University of China, Taiyuan.

articleTitle: A Multi-label Support Vector Machine-based Transformer Fault Prediction Method
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: Large power transformers typically use oil-immersed transformers, and the insulation oil can play a role in heat dissipation and insulation. By analyzing the gas composition in the oil, transformer failures can be predicted. Support vector machines are a data mining algorithm suitable for small sample data, but they are aimed at binary classification problems. However, there are multiple types of transformer failures. Therefore, a multi-label radial basis support vector machine is proposed for transformer failure prediction. The model analyzes gases with strong correlations among various gas content to construct a transformer failure prediction model. Machine learning algorithms can quickly mine potential rules in data, providing references for reasonable maintenance plans for transformers.

articleTitle: Feedback Attention Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: The hidden semantics are a crucial analysis element in the NLP field for performing tasks by analyzing the semantic context of text. Although self-attention mechanisms have achieved outstanding results in numerous tasks in recent years, their calculation solely based on input data results in excessive focus on the attention relationship between input data, reducing their ability to model contextual dependencies or develop global semantics and overall understanding. We have designed a novel feedback attention neural network architecture with a structure of hierarchical weight sharing, which enables distant interaction between the model's input and output layers and guides the calculation of input data attention based on the acquired global information. Through careful evaluation, we demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of our proposed model.

articleTitle: The Scheduling Analysis Method of Embedded Real-Time System Based on AADL-IO Annex
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: The embedded real-time system not only pays attention to the correctness of software task function, but also pays attention to the correctness of software task timing. There are a lot of IO resources in embedded real-time systems. The existing scheduling modeling and analysis methods are mainly aimed at tasks themself, without focusing IO resources. This paper proposes a scheduling analysis method of embedded real-time systems based on AADL-IO Annex. AADL-IO Annex is designed in two forms of meta-model and extended Backus paradigm. Scheduling analysis method of IO resources is based on time automata. Finally, a public embedded real-time system case is selected to verify the correctness and feasibility of the method in this paper. The method in this paper expands the modeling capabilities of AADL in terms of IO resources, and improves the fidelity of Scheduling analysis.

articleTitle: A Genetic Algorithm based Parallel Task Planning Method for Cooperative MRS
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: With in the trend of intelligence, task cooperation has been emerging as one main feature for Multiple Robot Systems (MRS) and applications, typically Multi-UAV (MUAV) system. For such swarm cooperative systems, how to plan and map their tasks to proper members within systems optimally and fast has been one vital issue that affects the efficiency of cooperation. So, in this article, a two-level task model is firstly established, which is the foundation of automatic task parsing and planning. Further, a Genetic Algorithm (GA) based Parallel Task Planning algorithm PTP-GA is proposed and designed, the goal of which is to improve the performance via cluster related tasks together and separating the dividing the solution space. Particularly, several constrained operators are designed to warrantee both the randomness and elitist individuals or segments. Finally, this proposed method is verified within a simulated scenario, and it shows that the performance of this parallel algorithm is indeed improved.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Distributed Video AI Super-Resolution Reconstruction System
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: This article proposes a distributed video AI super-resolution reconstruction solution based on MapReduce to address the issue of slow video super-resolution reconstruction in a single-machine environment. The solution utilizes scene detection algorithms and precise video segmentation algorithms to divide long videos into multiple video segments based on scenes. These segments are then assigned to different processing nodes for parallel processing, and finally merged to reduce the time required for video AI super-resolution reconstruction. Experimental results demonstrate that this solution effectively improves the speed of video AI super-resolution reconstruction. In addition, this article addresses the issues of low efficiency and low storage space utilization in the distributed storage system HDFS (Hadoop Distributed File System) when storing small files, specifically video segments. It proposes an optimized storage solution based on HDFS and Redis. This solution merges small files and constructs a small file merging and storage model on Redis, effectively alleviating the memory pressure on the NameNode in HDFS when storing a massive number of small files. Experimental results demonstrate that this solution sacrifices a certain degree of read/write performance but mitigates the rapid growth of NameNode memory. This solution holds significant theoretical and practical significance.

articleTitle: Improving Efficiency of Catastrophic Cascade Attacks by Combining Multi-attribute Node Influence
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: Infrastructures usually suffer environmental perturbations, and most of them are low probability events with catastrophic consequences, which poses a challenge to targeted preparedness for the possibility of cascading failures. The cascading failures on networks, in which malfunctioning nodes propagate failures through the reallocation process is studied in this paper. Traditional reallocation methods do not make use of global and local information reasonably, causing uneven distribution results. To conduct cascading attacks more efficiently, we propose a new strategy by considering node influence capability during the reallocation process, termed as RP-IC. The experimental results with respect to the node influence, network robustness as well as node destructiveness have demonstrated that our reallocation strategy RP-IC yields good performance on both synthetic and real networks, which can more efficiently expedite the cascade process than other traditional approaches.

articleTitle: Research on the Financing of College Students' Innovation and Entrepreneurship from the Perspective of Fusion Media
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: Innovation is the core driving force of national development, and the cultivation of innovative talents is an important measure to implement the strategy of strengthening national talents. Colleges and universities actively explore effective ways to cultivate innovative talents. Therefore, “mass entrepreneurship and innovation” has been widely promoted in colleges and universities in China. With the emergence of the Internet, big data, cloud computing and other technologies, the fusion media platform with the Internet as the carrier has emerged at the historic moment. The application of fusion media in the field of education is of great significance to the training of innovative talents in colleges and universities, and provides new opportunities and challenges for the entrepreneurial financing activities of college students. This paper uses the SWOT analysis method to analyze the influencing factors of the entrepreneurial financing activities of college students in the “Internet Plus” environment, constructs the SWOT matrix of college students' entrepreneurship financing, and analyzes the risk selection of financing methods under four different strategies combined with the financing selection theory. Finally, the paper puts forward the improvement suggestions of entrepreneurship and financing for college students based on the four-in-one media platform of “government, universities, society and college student entrepreneurs”.

Author Keywords: Fusion Media College Students Innovation and entrepreneurship Entrepreneurship financing

articleTitle: The Convergence of Digital Twin Technology and Personal Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: The concept of Digital Twin (DT) has now been applied to various sectors of human society and the trend of using is rapidly growing despite the fact that it requires vast digital infrastructure. Regardless of their physical counterparts, the ultimate goal of using DT is to improve the quality of human life and living environment. Even though, there are numerous application areas such as manufacturing, smart city, supply chain, retail, and healthcare, in this talk, Id like to focus more on healthcare sector starting out by discussing the convergence of the digital twin technologies and application of the technologies on healthcare especially on personal healthcare using IoT, networking technologies, standard based medical data, cybersecurity, and cloud computing. With such effort, DT will lead us to personalized precision medicine with less medical errors and the improvement of personal health.

articleTitle: Research on Information Dissemination and Digital Art
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: With the acceleration of technological progress and industrial transformation, the new generation of information technology represented by human intelligence, big data and other technologies is the cutting-edge technology that first penetrates into various areas of economic and social life. At the same time, combining digital information technology to deepen media integration and enhancing the effectiveness and influence of international communication has also become an important research and development direction in the field of media integration. In view of the fact that the current media education practice platform still needs to be developed, this paper proposes a construction method of the form and structure of the education practice platform based on the new trend of media integration, and divides the overall construction of the education practice platform into three parts: information dissemination, digital art and technical support. Aspects, and on this basis, an evaluation index system for digital art platforms is proposed. With cloud computing and big data as the core, it helps the development of metaverse, virtual image and other related digital art fields, controls the quality of the media education practice platform, and improves the international communication ability.

articleTitle: Discussion on Network Security under SDN Architecture
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: As a new network architecture, Software-defined network opens a new world for technical innovation and industrial development and provides a scalable and flexible solution for managing complex IoT. With the gradual maturity of SDN technology, the security issue has become the focus of recent academic research and industrial development. This article briefly introduces the SDN architecture and its application in the Internet of Things, aiming to identify structural defects caused by security issues in the system by analyzing the basic framework of SDN, and proposes a simple handling method at the end of the article. That is, focus on the plane security of station reporting control and the security of the north-south interface, limit the scope of security risks, and implement strict authorization and authentication mechanisms.

articleTitle: RoBGP: A Nested Biomedical Named Entity Recognition Method Based on RoBERTa and Global Pointer
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: Named entity recognition (NER) is one of the fundamental tasks in biomedical text mining, aiming to extract specific types of biomedical entities from texts. Compared to general-domain texts, biomedical texts often contain nested entities and local dependencies among entities, which pose challenges to existing NER models. To address these issues, we propose a nested biomedical NER method based on RoBERTa and Global Pointer (RoBGP). First, we dynamically obtain word-level semantic representations using the RoBERTa-wwm-ext-large model. Second, A BiLSTM model is used to capture long-distance semantic information in a bidirectional manner. Finally, we utilize a global pointer network to recognize all nested entities from innermost to outermost. Experimental results on the Chinese medical dataset CMeEE show that our method achieves the F1 score of 67.69%, outperforming other advanced models by 0.32% to 5.11%, validating the effectiveness of our approach in biomedical NER.

articleTitle: Named Entity Recognition in Electronic Medical Records Based on RoBERTa Embedding and BiLSTM-CRF
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: With the advent of the information age, electronic medical record resources are growing exponentially and have diverse data forms. In this paper, we propose SoftLexicon-RoBERTa-BiLSTM-CRFS (SLRBC) to implement electronic medical records named entity recognition. It can embed known lexical information into a character-level-based model to obtain lexical information, and yet avoid the impact of superposition errors caused by word-level-based models due to word separation. The pre-trained model RoBERTa enables the model to obtain a better embedding representation, which can effectively improve the accuracy of the model. We conduct experiments on the public datasets CCKS2018 and CCKS2019, and achieve better results to verify the effectiveness of the model.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of A High-Performance Rendering Algorithm for Large Terrain Systems based on GPU Parallel Computing
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: Although traditional 3D terrain algorithms can improve the rendering efficiency of the terrain, they often ignore the performance of the terrain itself. The use of four textures is not sufficient to deal with complex terrain scenes. Therefore, a terrain virtual texture mapping algorithm based on GPU instancing was proposed, which can map multiple surface textures of more terrains to one virtual texture before rendering, preventing the operation of GPU pipelines from being interrupted due to the change of surface textures. In this case, the parallel computing power of GPU can be better utilized, completing the efficient rendering of diverse terrains with fewer rendering times. The experimental results have shown that this algorithm can increase the diversity of terrain changes so as to applicable to more complex large terrain systems.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis of Hybrid Network Model
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: The existing text sentiment analysis models based on deep learning and neural network usually have problems such as incomplete text feature extraction and failure to consider the impact of key information on text sentiment tendency. Based on the parallel hybrid network and the two-way attention mechanism, an improved text sentiment analysis model is proposed. The model first takes the word vector trained by the BERT language model as the input, and then extracts the global and local features of the context simultaneously through the parallel hybrid neural network constructed by the Convolution Neural Network (CNN) and The Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU), so as to improve the feature extraction ability of the model. It also integrates the dual-way attention mechanism to strengthen the key information in the global feature and local feature, and the feature vectors obtained by feature fusion are used for sentiment analysis. The experimental results on the ChnSentiCorp hotel review data set and the NLPcc2013-NLPcc2014 microblog review data set show that the model has significantly improved the classification accuracy compared with the benchmark model.

articleTitle: OAM Pattern Recognition Method Based on ResNet-18 Migration Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: Aiming at the application of Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) in the field of optical communication, this paper proposes an OAM pattern recognition method based on ResNet-18 transfer learning. The OAM mode is a light wave with a spiral phase structure, which has the characteristics of high degree of freedom and large capacity, and has broad application prospects in the field of optical communication. However, detection and classification of OAM modes is difficult due to their complex wavefront structures. To address this issue, we use a pretrained ResNet-18 model to classify OAM patterns. This method uses the pre-trained ResNet-18 model for feature extraction and fine-tuning, which can effectively improve the classification performance of the model. Through experimental verification, the method has high accuracy and stability in the classification task of OAM mode. The research in this paper provides strong support for the application of OAM technology, and has certain reference value for image classification problems in other fields.

articleTitle: Improve Information Service Capabilities from Content Aggregation to Knowledge Provision with Generative Pre-trained Transformer (GPT)
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: The exponential growth of data and information has led to unprecedented opportunities and challenges in processing, analyzing, and utilizing this vast amount of knowledge. Nowadays, with the emerging and evolving of some novel strong Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies, especially GPT (short for Generative Pre-trained Transformer), it suddenly becomes possible for traditional information providers (such as Libraries, Data Intelligence Service Centers) to conduct business from resource and content aggregation to high-level knowledge provision. After analyzing the status of information businesses and mechanism of GPT, in this article, several possible changes and some corresponsive measures to achieve a higher intelligent level of knowledge service for traditional information providers are mainly discussed in depth. It's expected that such exploration will provide meaningful reference for facilitating the intelligent development of traditional information services.

articleTitle: Research on the Management Strategy of Marketing Personnel Loss Risk Based on Big Data Marketing
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: On the basis of big data marketing, this paper analyzes the relationship between the turnover risk of marketers and their individual value index, this paper puts forward different management strategies for individual value subdivision of marketing personnel: paying attention to high-risk and high-value personnel and low-risk and high-value personnel, and treating low-risk and low-value personnel cautiously according to the needs of enterprises, allowing or reducing high-risk low-value personnel.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Model for Railroad Structural Health Monitoring via Distributed Acoustic Sensing
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: Railway infrastructure plays a vital role in modern transportation systems, facilitating the efficient movement of people and goods. However, the integrity and performance of railroad structures are subject to various external forces and aging processes, which necessitate continuous monitoring to ensure safety and operational efficiency. This research focused on the structural health monitoring of the railroad using Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) data collected from a High Tonnage Loop (HTL). An investigation on applying a deep learning model, long-shot-term memory (LSTM), and gated recurrent Unit(GRU) is presented to identify and classify railroad conditions.

articleTitle: Service-oriented Intelligent OODA Loop
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: The OODA (Observe, Orient, Decide, Act) loop is a widely used decision-making model in various domains, including military operations, business strategy and cybersecurity. With the emergence of intelligent technologies, the intelligent OODA loop has gained increasing attention in recent years. However, the implementation of the intelligent OODA loop remains a challenging task as the intelligent algorithms introduce additional complexity in service implementation and service communication. To address this issue, this paper proposes to employ a service-oriented architecture for implementing the intelligent OODA loop. The proposed service-oriented intelligent OODA loop comprises several key components, including task decomposition, service description definition, intelligent service communication design, security and flow management strategies, and integration of necessary intelligent hardware. The proposed service-oriented intelligent OODA loop has the potential to provide significant benefits in improving speed, accuracy, scalability, cost-effectiveness and adaptability.

articleTitle: Research on Quality Model for Quantum Simulator Software
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: In recent years, the demand for arithmetic power from all walks of life is growing, especially the increasing popularity of AIGC, which makes people realize that huge technological progress cannot be made without the support of large arithmetic power. Quantum computing may bring a leap in computing power and become a ”trigger” and “catalyst” to accelerate the development of science and technology innovation, and its technical development trend and application prospects have become a hot issue of concern, and quantum simulators are a very important part of the development process. The development of quantum simulators is a very important part of the process. However, due to the lack of systematic evaluation theories and methods, it is difficult to quantify and analyze the quality of the increasing number of simulators on the market, which may hinder researchers from practicing their quantum algorithms objectively or developing quantum technologies. For these reasons, this paper proposes a quality model for quantum simulator software, which reflects the quality characteristics of simulators in seven aspects, such as functionality and performance efficiency, and selects some simulators for experimental validation of the proposed model to prove its rationality.

articleTitle: Honeytoken-Detector: A Symbolic Execution-Based Honeypot Token Detection Tool
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: Smart contracts have emerged as one of the most successful applications in the blockchain domain, playing a significant role in various blockchain ecosystems. Inspired by smart contracts, a multitude of cryptographic assets have been created. To standardize these assets, industry standards such as ERC20 (Ethereum Request for Comments 20), ERC721, and ERC1155 have been proposed. In recent years, smart contracts have frequently fallen victim to attacks. Honeypot contracts, disguised as ERC20-compliant tokens, are widely prevalent on the blockchain, enticing victims to make purchases. Such malicious smart contracts exhibiting deceptive behavior are collectively referred to as honeypot tokens. This paper focuses on ERC20-compliant smart contracts and defines six common types of honeypot issues. Building upon advancements in smart contract vulnerability detection, we propose an enhanced symbolic execution-based detection tool called Honeytoken-Detector. We conduct experiments on both contracts known to have similar issues and actual token contracts from the real world. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our tool in identifying vulnerabilities.

articleTitle: Efficient MIH/SDN-Based Vertical Handover for 5G HetNets
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: Ultra-densification is one of the 5G and beyond (B5G) networks solutions to increase data rate and network capacity. The perception of this technology is based on the construction of a large number of small cells in a specific area which may include different Radio Access Technologies (RATs) such as LTE-advanced, C-IoT (Cellular Internet of Thing), Narrowband-IoT (NB-IoT) and 5G WiFi in a unified wireless heterogeneous system based on an IP core network infrastructure. The deployment of small cells generates a good connection following the provision of shorter distance between cell access point and the mobile node which in turn serve to reduce the signal attenuation and noise. The downside of the densification on B5G is that poses challenges for the mobility management, including frequent unnecessary and ping-pong handovers, with additional problems related to increased delay, energy efficiency and total failure of the handover process. This paper proposes an integrated B5G networks architecture using the Software Defined Networking (SDN) and Media (MIH) paradigms and provides an optimized vertical handover process reached by an efficient network selection algorithm. Simulation results validate the efficiency of our proposal.

articleTitle: Exploring the Current Landscape and Future Directions of Information Technology in Dance Education
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: Dance education has undergone significant changes with the integration of information technology. Traditional dance pedagogy is now complemented by innovative digital software tools and applications. This work surveys the diverse applications of information technology in dance education at college or university level and the impact it has on teaching and learning processes. We discuss the integration of technology in various aspects of dance education, including skill development, choreography, performance analysis, VR/AR, online virtual learning, and collaborative learning. Additionally, the benefits and challenges associated with the use of information technology are also examined and the future research directions for research and practice in this field are proposed.

articleTitle: Aspect Level Sentiment Analysis with CNN Bi-LSTM and Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel neural network model for aspect-level sentiment analysis that combines CNN, Bi-LSTM, and attention mechanisms. The aim is to enhance the effectiveness of sentiment analysis specifically when dealing with sentences containing aspect terms. The main goal is to identify the keywords or elements that contribute to predicting sentiment. Traditional sentiment analysis models often struggle to capture the varying sentiments within sentences treating them uniformly. These models tend to treat the sentence as an entity and overlook the significance of where aspect terms are positioned within the sentence. This limitation significantly impacts the precision of sentiment analysis since sentiments, towards aspects can differ significantly within a single sentence. However, this model addresses that issue by combining CNN, Bi-LSTM and attention mechanisms. CNNs focus on features to identify keywords related to aspects while Bi-LSTM considers the overall context through bidirectional processing enabling a comprehensive understanding of aspect sentiments. Additionally, the attention mechanism enhances the analysis by focusing on words and assigning weights according to their significance. This refinement significantly enhances prediction accuracy. The proposed model is evaluated using the SemEval 2014 datasets, which contain restaurant and laptop reviews. It showcases progress in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency when compared to existing sentiment models. The novel neural network model discussed in this paper represents a progress, in analyzing sentiment at the aspect level. The model accurately identifies keywords associated with specific aspect terms, taking into consideration their positions within the sentence.

articleTitle: Research on Domain Knowledge Representation Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: Knowledge is the fruit of human's knowledge of the objective world in practice and the crystallization of wisdom. A knowledge base makes a knowledge-based system (or expert system) intelligent by structuring and sorting out knowledge in a specific field and storing, organizing, managing and using it in a computer using a scientific knowledge representation. Based on the research of knowledge base construction in securities industry, this paper first summarizes and explains several representative knowledge representation models. Then, it summarizes the application scenarios of common knowledge representation techniques in the fields of product design, robot control, and natural language processing. In addition, based on the investigation of the knowledge characteristics of the securities industry, a knowledge representation model of the securities industry based on 5W1lH is proposed to organize and manage the multimodal information resources and provide high-value information for user needs, while the knowledge representation technology of the mechanical industry based on hypergraph embedding is examined and the specific processes and application scenarios are summarized.

articleTitle: Business Scenario Driven Reinforcement Learning Testing Method
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: Reinforcement learning has been successfully applied in software testing, but the existing testing methods cannot perform effective testing according to the characteristics of applications, and using outdated interactive experience during training, resulting in inefficient testing. In this paper, we propose BSDRTesting. Firstly, the demonstration experience of human users is collected according to the functional scenarios and business logic of each application, and combining reinforcement learning and imitation learning to maximize rewards while imitating user behavior, experience replay aims to sample experiences from the agent's self-exploration and expert demonstrations to improve sampling efficiency. At the same time, according to the input rules, the black-box testing method is used to fully test the input events, and finally an experience filtering mechanism is proposed, and the reward value and TD-Error are used as the basis for priority sampling. The experimental results on 10 open source applications show BSDRTesting has achieved significant improvements in code coverage and branch coverage compared with existing methods.

articleTitle: Research on the Distributed Secure Storage of Embedded Terminals Based on the Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: The blockchain is a distributed public ledger technology that originates from the digital crypto currency bitcoin. Blockchain's key advantages include decentralization, time-series data, collective maintenance, programmability and security. It breaks through the limitation of traditional center-based technology and has broad military development prospect. Nevertheless, with the distributed embedded devices in the battlefield in the future, the cooperative computing task needs to be performed effectively and rapidly among them. Furthermore, in order to achieve the aim of the cooperative computation on the multi-device, the urgent and primary problem is how to realize the effective share and secure storage about the critical data. Consequently, given the requirement of data sharing, the architecture design of data distributed secure storage based on the blockchain is proposed in this paper. Besides, the vivid descriptions of some key functional modules are given.

articleTitle: Design of Airborne Intelligent Computing System Oriented to Intelligent Task Processing
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence technology promotes the gradual evolution of the “three integration” of mechanization, informatization and intelligence. The mass data characteristics of airborne mission informatization put forward higher demands on the storage, transmission and management capabilities of airborne data. The characteristics of high complexity, strong confrontation, strong real-time, and uncertainty of airborne intelligent tasks pose more challenges to the intelligent processing of airborne data. This paper analyzes the data characteristics and mission characteristics in the process of airborne intelligence missions, and proposes an airborne intelligent computing architecture for airborne data processing of intelligent missions. The composition and function of each technical layer are expounded, and several problems of airborne intelligent computing technology are analyzed. Finally, the development trend of airborne intelligent technology development is prospected.

articleTitle: Multi-Head Self-Attention Network for Multi-View Deep Clustering
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: Multi-view clustering comprehensively processes data objects by studying different views or modalities, as well as the differences or complementary information between different views, then classifies the data objects into different groups by unsupervised learning. However, most of the work these days fuses the information of multiple views only after rough processing, which ignores the difference of information value among different data features in the process of deep fusion representation. In this paper, we propose a Multi-head Self-attention network for Deep Clustering (MSDC) to highlight valuable information features and improve the effect of multi-view clustering. Comprehensive experiments have been carried out on real world datasets and results show that MSDC outperforms other advanced baselines, demonstrating that MSDC provides an excellent approach for multi-view clustering.

articleTitle: Multi-Request Data Cache Optimization Strategy in Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: With the rapid growth in the number of mobile devices, more and more data is created and requested by users. By caching the data to the edge server, users can obtain the content they request in a closer place, which reduces the network load and improves the user experience. However, existing articles only focus on a single request of users, while users often request multiple content at one time, which leads to more complex caching scenarios. In this paper, we will study an edge data cache scenario with multiple requests, and design a cost function to optimize the cache results. In this paper, we formulate the data cache problem as a mixed integer programming problem and minimize our cost function. Extensive experiments are conducted on a real-world dataset that contains the locations of edge servers and mobile users, and the results reveal that our approach significantly outperform the baseline approaches.

articleTitle: Video Copy Detection Based on Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: In recent years, the number of pirated videos has soared, which has brought great damage to the interests of the original. Video copy detection technology can solve such problems to some extent, but the detection process of traditional video copy detection technology is not open, so that the detection results are not convincing. Based on this, this paper proposes an open, transparent and verifiable video copy detection method based on blockchain technology to ensure the transparency and openness of the results. The smart contract is called on the chain for automatic copyright detection, and the video characteristic value is permanently immutable saved on the block chain to ensure the originality of copyright works and the verifiability of detection results. In similarity comparison, the method of slice comparison can greatly shorten the comparison time, which is 1/50 of the traditional comparison time. Experimental results show that this method is very effective in retrieving similar images and detecting the similarity between original and pirated videos.

articleTitle: A Fact-Searching and Matching System Based on News Content About COVID-19
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: With the global outbreak of the novel coronavirus, China has also been seriously affected, and news reports about the epidemic have flooded the internet. For some vulnerable groups and the general public, identifying the authenticity of the epidemic news content remains to be studied. This paper mainly addresses how to obtain effective knowledge of COVID-19 in the epidemic news content, and determines the optimal semantic model of retrieval and matching by means of multi-model fusion. Finally, the retrieval and matching system is constructed to obtain the best-matched news content in the form of fact questions. Based on the above scenarios, the main research contents of this paper include the construction of the COVID-19 fact knowledge map and research on multi-model fusion of fact question and answer retrieval and matching. In order to obtain the best fact matching more accurately, the basic Word2vec, BERT model, and unsupervised SimCSE two-tower model are selected in this paper. And the optimal semantic model is determined through the weighted fusion of the three models, as well as the construction of the fact retrieval and matching system of COVID-19 news content. Combined with the above research content, the main fact retrieval model of the system is constructed to obtain the sorted epidemic fact question-and-answer data as the main knowledge source. For the general COVID-19 fact issues, such as pneumonia symptoms, and treatment opinions, a fact retrieval and matching system based on the COVID-19 news content has been preliminarily realized.

articleTitle: An Empirical Study on Scrum Deviations in Organizations with Software Development
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: Scrum is one of the most popular agile software development frameworks. As a guideline to help development teams to work effectively to achieve development goals, Scrum Guide is provided. In practice, many organizations do not strictly follow the Scrum Guide, causing Scrum deviations. The objective of this research is to gather Scrum deviations data and analyze the impact and factors that cause Scrum deviations in Scrum Teams. Via the interviews with the Scrum Teams from IT departments of different sizes and types of software development and in different organizations in Thailand, 19 Scrum deviations were identified. These deviations were then used in an online questionnaire to collect the impact of Scrum deviations on Scrum Teams. The results show that the deviations do not necessarily have a negative impact on the Scrum Teams and their organizations, as certain deviations are even beneficial. However, there is no statistical difference in the deviating behavior of the Scrum Teams from IT departments of different sizes and different types of software development. Also, the major cause of the deviating behavior is the Scrum Teams themselves, as the teams tend to adjust Scrum activities to better suit team practices.

articleTitle: The Intellectualized Disposal System of Cognitive Domain's Confrontation
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: In recent years, the confrontational behavior in cognitive domain have gradually developed from fragmented and local behavior such as guided propaganda and agitation to widely influencing global confrontational behavior. The impact of confrontational behaviors act in cognitive domain is even worse. Vicious cognitive domain events occurred in our society are more frequent these years. Problems created by cognitive domain's confrontation are worthy to explore and research from the perspective of artificial intelligence and system science. In view of this, we try to build an intellectualized disposal system to give a solution for these problems. The main work is as follows: (1)We build the framework required for the disposal of cognitive domain's confrontation based on the OODA loop and confrontational strategy theory. We analyze the characteristics and methods of cognitive domain's confrontation from actual cases. (2)We construct an intelligent solution to the problems of cognitive domain confrontation hierarchically, and analyze its engineering feasibility based on existing artificial intelligence methods such as natural language processing. (3)We presents the design of the Intellectualized Disposal System of Cognitive Domain's Confrontation(IDSoCDC), which is introduced in this paper.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis and Prognosis Modeling Methods in Predictive Maintenance: A Systematic Review
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: Intelligent manufacturing approaches, technologies, and procedures have grown increasingly with the emergence of Industry 4.0 and smart manufacturing. Machines and managers, in the manufacturing process, must make decisions based on a massive amount of data and customization on regular basis. One of the most essential concerns in this scope is the ability to predict the requirement for asset maintenance at a specific future time. The predictive maintenance (PdM) function helps in the early detection of flaws and errors in machinery before they progress to critical stages; reducing hence machine downtime and associated expenses. Therefore, multiple techniques have emerged as a viable tool in PdM applications for preventing problems in the equipment that makes up the factory floor's production lines. The purpose of this paper is to give a thorough literature review of PdM methods, highlighting which are currently being considered and the performance of current state-of-the-art predictive maintenance strategies. This review focuses on six scientific databases and provides a valuable foundation for PdM methodologies, their key outcomes, obstacles, potential, as well as supporting new research in the field.

articleTitle: An Approach for Constructing Multi-Modal Spatio-Temporal Ontology of Ship Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: Ship communication situational analysis is an important component of current maritime traffic management. However, it faces some challenges and difficulties. Firstly, the heterogeneity and diversity of ship communication data make data integration and analysis difficult. Secondly, traditional data analysis methods often ignore the spatio-temporal relationships and contextual information between data, resulting in inaccurate and incomplete analysis results. In addition, existing ship communication situational analysis methods often only consider single-modal data, which cannot fully reflect the multi-modal characteristics of maritime traffic. To address these issues, we propose a ship communication situational analysis method based on a multi-modal spatio-temporal knowledge graph. This method can effectively integrate heterogeneous data and model and analyze spatio-temporal relationships and contextual information between data, thus achieving more accurate and comprehensive situational analysis. In conclusion, a multi-modal spatio-temporal knowledge graph is an effective method for ship communication situational analysis, which can overcome the current challenges and difficulties and provide more accurate and comprehensive data support for maritime traffic management.

articleTitle: Cohesive Group Emotion Recognition using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: Emotions are pivotal in shaping social dynamics and interactions. An in-depth grasp of the emotions within a group setting can offer valuable insights into group cohesion and the overall emotional atmosphere, thereby bolstering effective communication, teamwork, and collaboration. This study introduces an innovative methodology designed to predict the collective emotions of a group exclusively from an image. Leveraging advanced deep learning techniques, our approach transcends previous methods that treat groups as homogeneous entities. Instead, it acknowledges the diverse spectrum of emotions within a group, capturing the distinct emotional expressions of each individual. To facilitate this, we harnessed cutting-edge deep learning techniques encompassing face detection and pre-trained emotion recognition models. A custom dataset was meticulously curated through web-scraping, manual photography, and Google’s FEC (Facial Emotion Comparison) dataset. Our research entailed the utilization of models such as YOLOv3, HaarCascade, and SSD for precise face detection in images. Subsequently, we employed pre-trained DeepFace and FER models to predict seven distinct emotions for each individual featured in the image. Comprehensive evaluations encompassed metrics such as cross-entropy losses among emotions and sample analyses, culminating in an impressive top-3 accuracy rate of approximately 90%. These findings underscore the effectiveness of deep learning in accurately predicting emotions from group images, thereby enhancing communication and collaboration across diverse contexts. This research signifies a substantial breakthrough by pioneering an approach that deconstructs group images to individuate emotional recognition, yielding a more nuanced comprehension of group dynamics and promoting improved social interactions.

articleTitle: Detection of New Crown Epidemic Rumors Based on Knowledge Graph
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: Since the outbreak of the new crown epidemic, a large amount of epidemic-related information has emerged on the Internet, including many false information and rumors, which may mislead the public and pose a potential threat to public health and social security. Therefore, in the context of the new crown epidemic, how to automate the rumor detection and identification of rumor information has become an important issue that cannot be ignored. In this context, this paper integrates and improves several mainstream deep learning models to achieve rumor identification by introducing the entity representation of external knowledge, and the main work contents are: new crown rumor detection model based on knowledge graph, new crown epidemic rumor detection system, and construction of new crown rumor dataset. In this paper, a directed heterogeneous document graph is constructed for the text to be tested, subject and entity information are introduced, structured and unstructured feature extraction is performed for external information, entity features based on external knowledge are obtained, and entity comparison is carried out through the entity comparison network, and finally the rumor detection results are obtained. Based on the above new crown rumor detection model, this paper designs and implements a new crown epidemic rumor detection system to assist users in identifying the authenticity of new crown epidemic news. In addition, this paper constructs the latest COVID-19 Rumor Dataset (CRD), including 24915 rumor data and 9995 non-rumor data, including a total of 34910 data, which has the advantages of large data volume, high timeliness and rich themes.

articleTitle: Robust Zero-watermarking Algorithm for Medical Images Based on ORB and DCT
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: With the rapid development of the Internet technology field, the use of the Internet to transmit medical images has gradually become an efficient and convenient transmission method. It improves the efficiency of medical services, which allows medical institutions and doctors to share medical images and diagnostic information quickly. However, there are also some potential security risks in the transmission of medical images on the Internet, and data leakage and data tampering occur frequently. This paper proposes a zero-watermarking algorithm for medical images based on Oriented FAST and Rotated BRIEF (ORB) and Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) to solve the above problems. Firstly, this algorithm is used to extract the feature vector of the medical image, and then the feature sequence of the medical image is obtained by combining the perceptual hashing algorithm, and the logistic map is used to perform chaotic scrambling encryption on the watermark image. Finally, the zero-watermarking technology is used to embed and extract the watermark. The experimental results show that the algorithm can effectively extract and restore the watermark under conventional attacks and geometric attacks and can effectively protect the information security of medical images, and the algorithm has good robustness and invisibility, which has a particular development prospect in the field of medical images.

articleTitle: Chinese Text Correction System Based on Ernie
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: Nowadays, Internet technology is developing at a high speed, which makes the vast number of Internet users constantly producing and receiving huge amounts of information data. Because of the low threshold of Internet use, it leads to the uneven quality of information on the Internet, and the quality of most of the information is decreasing. The quality of information can be improved by proofreading the text for errors. Therefore, it is important to detect and correct typos in text information. With the more widespread application of deep learning in the field of natural language processing, a deep learning and rule-based approach to Chinese text detection and error correction has achieved better results in processing text compared to traditional methods. The main work is as follows: the existing deep learning algorithms and models on text error correction are compiled, briefly introduced and compared, in which the effect of Ernie and Bert-based Chinese error correction processing is mainly compared, laying the foundation for selecting the ernie end-to-end Chinese error correction model. The error correction process of the Ernie model is also introduced, and the prediction results are evaluated and trained on the selected dataset. After experimental validation, the Ernie-based end-to-end model achieves better results with a greater improvement in accuracy. Moreover, the front-end interface design was carried out, and the Chinese text error correction system was successfully built, which can perform functions such as uploading and downloading of files, and support the saving of results.

articleTitle: HybridSeqNet: A Multimodal Approach Incorporating Convolutional and Long Short-Term Memory Networks for Comprehensive Structural Protein Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: In the field of bioinformatics and molecular biology, the accurate classification of proteins based on their sequences plays a crucial role in understanding their functions and interactions. This research paper presents a novel deep learning architecture, named HybridSeqNet, that leverages the strengths of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Long Short-Term Memory Networks (LSTMs) to enhance the accuracy of protein structure classification from sequence data. The proposed HybridSeqNet architecture capitalizes on the hierarchical features captured by CNNs in local regions of protein structure sequences and the temporal dependencies captured by LSTMs in longer-range contexts. This joint architecture synergistically integrates these two neural network paradigms, enabling the model to effectively learn intricate patterns within protein sequences. The dataset used contained more than 4,00,000 protein structure sequences. Various types of protein structures like DNA, RNA, hybrid DNA-RNA, etc. are considered for classification. We also compare our model with various existing models. HybridSeqNet achieves remarkable classification accuracy of 92.86% when compared to traditional models. The architecture’s effectiveness is demonstrated through comprehensive experiments on a huge dataset of protein structure sequences.

articleTitle: Robust Zero-watermarking Algorithm for Medical Images Based on GFTT-KAZE and DCT
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: As medical technology advances, medical images are becoming increasingly important in diagnosis and therapy. However, due to the potential repercussions of leaking or tampering, which could jeopardize patient privacy and treatment, the protection and management of medical images has become a critical concern. As a result, ensuring the encryption and confidentiality of medical images has become critical. Based on GFTT-KAZE-DCT, this research provides a strong digital watermarking system for medical photos. To begin, the GFTT (Good Features to Track) method is used to extract feature points from medical pictures. To describe the feature points, the KAZE method is used, resulting in a feature descriptor matrix. Perceptual hashing is used to further process the initial image. The feature matrix created by the KAZE descriptor is then subjected to DCT (Discrete Cosine Transform). The coefficient matrix generated by DCT is used to acquire the desired eigenvector. To better resist geometric and conventional attacks, the watermark is flexibly integrated with chaos encryption technology, hash function, and the “third-party concept.” In conclusion, our algorithm provides an effective way for protecting the privacy and integrity of medical images. It incorporates advanced techniques such as GFTT-KAZE-DCT and perceptual hash, and it can withstand a variety of attacks.

articleTitle: Robust Zero-Watermarking Algorithm for Medical Images Based on AGAST-LATCH and DCT
publicationTitle: 2023 26th ACIS International Winter Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD-Winter)
abstract: Medical image transmission is an important aspect of digital healthcare. However, security and privacy are crucial issues during this process. Traditional watermarking techniques have become unreliable due to the damage they cause to pixel information in images. To solve this problem, zero-watermarking technology has emerged. Compared to traditional watermarking technology, zero-watermarking does not affect the visibility and quality of medical images and has higher robustness against attacks. Based on this, a robust zero-watermarking algorithm for medical images based on AGAST-LATCH and DCT is proposed in this paper. First, the AGAST algorithm and LATCH algorithm are combined to extract the feature matrix of the medical image. Then, the hash sequences of the medical image are obtained using Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) and perceptual hashing algorithm on the feature matrix. The resulting hash sequence is combined with the encrypted watermark information, which is encrypted by the chaotic state of Logistic Map to enhance the robustness of the watermark information. Finally, a zero-watermarking technique is employed to create a watermark that is resistant to both conventional and geometric attacks.
